title: Advance Economic Indicators Report (advance goods trade, retail & wholesale inventories, Nov 2026 data)
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html lists 'Advance Economic Indicators Report (International Trade, Retail, & Wholesale) | December 28, 2026 | 8:30 AM | November 2026' (fetched direct 2026-09-05); the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx (fetched direct 2026-09-05) independently schedules a 2026-12-28 08:30 GDPNow posting naming 'Advance Economic Indicators'. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit, and because the funding exposure below is precisely a reason not to treat the date as settled
notes: THE FUNDING-EXPOSED EDITION OF THIS SERIES, and the reason it is worth a row rather than the ordinary calendar noise a quarterly successor would be. H.R. 6500 (signed 2026-09-02) funds the government only through 2026-12-11; this release lands 17 days past that cliff. What makes the exposure different from durable-goods-2026-12-23's - the sibling row filed for the same cliff - is the failure mode. On this exact series' measured 2026 precedent Census DELETES rather than delays: the January 2026 and February 2026 reference months still read 'Suspended' on the Census calendar and were never published, while December 2025 data merely slipped 1/28 to 2/19 under a Census bulletin whose own wording is 'delayed due to the recent lapse in federal funding'. Advance durable goods, by contrast, delayed ~27-29 days and lost nothing. So the honest label on this edition is MAY NOT EXIST, not may be late - and a deleted edition is not recoverable information, unlike a late one. That matters downstream because this report is the GDP nowcast's composition engine (measured in the 10-28 ledger: 12.2x the composition churn of an ordinary GDPNow vintage, 132x on the net-exports line), so a deletion blinds the Q4 nowcast's trade and inventory lines rather than postponing them. CONSIDERED AND DECLINED alongside this one: advance-economic-indicators-2026-11-27 (October data), which sits inside the CR window and whose only claim is that a macro print precedes the 12-09 FOMC - the generic argument this calendar's bar rejects; its absence is a decision, not an oversight. Not a tradeable print on its own (symbols: [], no house playbook is macro-keyed). Discovered during the advance-economic-indicators-2026-10-28 initial research (2026-09-05).
